h1: Types of commercial cleaning: definitions, uses, and the industries that need them
metaTitle: Types of Commercial Cleaning: Definitions and Uses | ECC
metaDescription: Twenty types of commercial cleaning defined, with what each covers, which industries use it, and how often it is scheduled. A reference guide.
cutToTheChase: Commercial cleaning is the paid, contracted cleaning of non-residential buildings. It splits into roughly twenty distinct service types, each with its own scope, frequency, and regulatory context. The four that cover most buildings are janitorial services, office cleaning, deep cleaning, and floor care. The rest are specialist work triggered by an industry requirement, a building condition, or a one-time event.
atAGlance: Janitorial services is the recurring baseline. Everything else is either scheduled on top of it or replaces it in a specialist setting.
Cleaning, sanitizing, and disinfecting are three different outcomes with three different standards, and the words are not interchangeable.
Regulated settings such as healthcare, food service, and childcare pull the cleaning scope into a compliance document rather than a service list.
Frequency is set by traffic, soil type, and regulation, not by building size.
Most commercial contracts combine one recurring type with two or three periodic types on a quarterly or annual cycle.

typesIntro: Each entry below gives the definition, what the work covers, the industries that buy it, and how often it is normally scheduled.

types.name: Janitorial services
types.definition: Janitorial services are recurring, scheduled cleaning of a commercial building under contract, covering the routine tasks that keep a facility usable day to day.
covers: Floors swept, vacuumed, and damp mopped
Restrooms cleaned and restocked
Trash and recycling removed
High-touch points disinfected
Common areas, entries, and break rooms reset
types.industries: Offices, schools, medical buildings, industrial sites, retail, religious facilities, municipal buildings
types.frequency: Nightly, or two to five nights per week

types.name: Office cleaning
types.definition: Office cleaning is janitorial work scoped specifically to workplace environments, with the emphasis on desks, shared equipment, meeting rooms, kitchens, and restrooms.
covers: Desk surfaces, shared keyboards, and phones wiped
Conference rooms reset between uses
Kitchen and break room surfaces, sinks, and appliance exteriors
Entry glass, reception, and lobby floors
Restroom cleaning and consumables restocking
types.industries: Professional services, finance, insurance, legal, technology, coworking spaces, corporate headquarters
types.frequency: Nightly or several nights per week, after hours

types.name: Day porter services
types.definition: A day porter is a cleaner stationed in a building during operating hours to handle spills, restrooms, entries, and visible problems as they happen rather than overnight.
covers: Restroom checks and restocking through the day
Spill and incident response
Lobby, entry, and elevator upkeep during peak traffic
Trash in high-use areas such as cafes and conference floors
Event and meeting room turnover
types.industries: Class A office buildings, hospitals, airports, universities, large retail, stadiums, conference centers
types.frequency: Daily during business hours, often a fixed shift

types.name: Commercial deep cleaning
types.definition: Commercial deep cleaning is an intensive, scheduled clean that reaches the surfaces routine nightly work does not, including behind and underneath fixed equipment.
covers: Furniture moved and cleaned underneath
Walls, doors, frames, and baseboards washed
Vents, light fixtures, and high surfaces dusted
Floors machine scrubbed or refinished
Restrooms descaled and grout cleaned
types.industries: Every commercial sector, commonly offices, schools, restaurants, medical, and manufacturing
types.frequency: Quarterly, semiannually, or at seasonal breaks

types.name: Disinfection services
types.definition: Disinfection services apply an EPA-registered product to surfaces for the contact time its label requires, in order to kill specified pathogens rather than simply remove soil.
covers: Surface cleaning first, then disinfectant application
High-touch point treatment across the building
Electrostatic or fogging application for large or irregular areas
Product selection matched to the target organism
Documented coverage and dwell time
types.industries: Healthcare, schools, childcare, gyms, food service, offices during outbreak periods
types.frequency: Added to nightly work, or on demand after an outbreak

types.name: Medical facility cleaning
types.definition: Medical facility cleaning is infection-control cleaning of clinical buildings, using zoned risk levels, color-coded equipment, registered disinfectants, and written documentation of each room.
covers: Risk zoning from administrative areas to procedure rooms
Color-coded cloths and single-room mop heads
High-touch disinfection with recorded dwell times
Waiting rooms, restrooms, and corridors
Room-by-room completion logs
types.industries: Hospitals, outpatient clinics, dental and specialist practices, dialysis centers, imaging centers, veterinary clinics
types.frequency: Nightly, with periodic deep work on a quarterly cycle

types.name: Terminal cleaning
types.definition: Terminal cleaning is a full top-to-bottom clean and disinfection of a clinical room, including walls, fixtures, curtains, and every horizontal surface, performed when the room is emptied.
covers: All removable items stripped out
Walls, fixtures, and curtains cleaned
Every horizontal surface disinfected to label contact time
Floor cleaned last, edges included
Completion documented before the room returns to use
types.industries: Hospitals, surgical centers, isolation units, procedure suites, laboratories
types.frequency: On isolation room release, or on a set procedure room cycle

types.name: Post-construction cleaning
types.definition: Post-construction cleaning removes construction dust, debris, adhesive, and protective coverings from a newly built or renovated space so it can be occupied.
covers: Rough clean of debris during the build
Fine clean of dust from every surface including ledges and vents
Sticker, adhesive, paint, and compound removal from glass and fixtures
Floor protection removal and first finish application
Final detail clean before handover
types.industries: General contractors, developers, property managers, commercial landlords, retail fit-outs, medical buildouts
types.frequency: One-time, usually in two or three staged visits

types.name: Commercial floor care
types.definition: Commercial floor care is the maintenance of hard floors through scrubbing, stripping, refinishing, burnishing, and sealing, separate from routine mopping.
covers: Machine scrubbing to lift embedded soil
Stripping old finish back to the substrate
Applying and curing new floor finish coats
Burnishing for gloss and wear resistance
Sealing concrete and porous surfaces
types.industries: Schools, retail, healthcare, warehouses, offices, religious facilities, municipal buildings
types.frequency: Burnishing monthly, strip and refinish annually or semiannually

types.name: Carpet cleaning and extraction
types.definition: Commercial carpet cleaning uses hot water extraction or encapsulation to pull soil out of carpet fiber, which vacuuming alone cannot remove.
covers: Pre-treatment of traffic lanes and spots
Hot water extraction or encapsulation
Spot and stain treatment
Drying and airflow management
Protective treatment where specified
types.industries: Offices, hotels, conference centers, schools, churches, theaters, residential property common areas
types.frequency: Semiannually or annually, with spot work as needed

types.name: Tile and grout cleaning
types.definition: Tile and grout cleaning mechanically removes soil and grease from porous grout lines that mopping spreads rather than lifts.
covers: Alkaline or degreasing pre-treatment
Mechanical agitation of grout lines
High pressure rinse and extraction
Grout color restoration where needed
Sealing to slow resoiling
types.industries: Restaurants, commercial kitchens, restrooms in any sector, locker rooms, retail entries, healthcare
types.frequency: Quarterly to annually depending on grease load

types.name: Commercial window cleaning
types.definition: Commercial window cleaning covers interior and exterior glass, frames, and sills on commercial buildings, including access work above ground level.
covers: Interior glass, frames, and sills
Exterior ground level glass and entries
Pole or lift access for upper floors
Mineral and hard water stain treatment
Screen and track cleaning
types.industries: Retail storefronts, offices, car dealerships, restaurants, medical buildings, hotels
types.frequency: Monthly or quarterly for storefronts, semiannually for upper floors

types.name: High dusting and high ceiling cleaning
types.definition: High dusting removes accumulated dust from surfaces above normal reach, including beams, duct runs, light fixtures, sprinkler heads, and ceiling decks.
covers: Structural steel, beams, and joists
Duct exteriors and vent grilles
Light fixtures and sprinkler heads
Ceiling decks and upper wall surfaces
Lift or pole access with containment below
types.industries: Warehouses, manufacturing plants, gyms, churches, schools, food production facilities
types.frequency: Annually, or semiannually in dusty production settings

types.name: Warehouse and industrial cleaning
types.definition: Warehouse and industrial cleaning handles large-footprint facilities where the soil is dust, tire marks, oil, and production residue rather than office soil.
covers: Ride-on scrubbing of aisles and dock areas
Dock door, bay, and loading area cleaning
Racking and high dusting
Oil and tire mark removal
Break room, restroom, and office cleaning inside the facility
types.industries: Distribution centers, third party logistics, manufacturing, food production, cold storage, automotive
types.frequency: Nightly or several nights per week, with periodic deep work

types.name: Restaurant and commercial kitchen cleaning
types.definition: Restaurant cleaning covers front of house, restrooms, and back of house degreasing, and is distinct from the hood and duct cleaning that falls under NFPA 96.
covers: Dining room, bar, and entry floors and surfaces
Restrooms cleaned fixture by fixture
Back of house wall and equipment exterior degreasing
Quarry tile and grout deep cleaning
Trash and grease area wash down
types.industries: Restaurants, bars, cafes, hotel kitchens, corporate dining, school and hospital cafeterias, breweries
types.frequency: Nightly for front of house, monthly to quarterly for degreasing

types.name: School and education facility cleaning
types.definition: School cleaning services combine daily custodial work during term with outbreak response and intensive deep cleaning during scheduled breaks.
covers: Classrooms, corridors, and restrooms nightly
High-touch disinfection during illness season
Gym floors, locker rooms, and mats
Cafeteria dining areas and hard floors
Strip, wax, and classroom resets at term breaks
types.industries: Public school districts, private and charter schools, universities, trade schools, daycare and childcare centers
types.frequency: Nightly in term, with deep cleaning at February, April, and summer breaks

types.name: Retail store cleaning
types.definition: Retail cleaning keeps a sales floor presentable during trading hours and resets it overnight, with the emphasis on entries, floors, fitting rooms, and restrooms.
covers: Entry matting, glass, and door handles
Sales floor hard floor or carpet maintenance
Fitting rooms and mirrors
Customer restrooms
Stock room and back of house areas
types.industries: Shopping centers, big box retail, grocery, pharmacy, convenience stores, showrooms, car dealerships
types.frequency: Nightly, with day porter coverage in larger formats

types.name: Hospitality and hotel cleaning
types.definition: Hospitality cleaning covers the public and back of house areas of hotels and venues, separate from the housekeeping team that services guest rooms.
covers: Lobby, reception, and corridor floors
Meeting and banquet space turnover
Public restrooms through the day
Fitness and pool area surfaces
Back of house, staff areas, and service corridors
types.industries: Hotels, conference centers, banquet halls, event venues, private clubs, casinos
types.frequency: Daily, with day porter coverage and periodic deep work

types.name: Event cleaning
types.definition: Event cleaning is one-time cleaning scheduled before, during, and after a gathering, sized to the crowd rather than the building.
covers: Pre-event setup clean and restroom staging
During-event restroom checks and trash rotation
Spill and incident response
Post-event breakdown, floor clearing, and trash removal
Full reset of the venue for next use
types.industries: Conference centers, stadiums, festivals, corporate functions, trade shows, weddings, municipal events
types.frequency: One-time, scheduled around the event

types.name: Property turnover cleaning
types.definition: Turnover cleaning returns a vacated commercial or residential unit to a leasable condition between tenants.
covers: Full unit clean including appliances and cabinetry interiors
Floor cleaning or refinishing
Window, blind, and fixture cleaning
Debris and abandoned item removal
Final inspection detail before showing
types.industries: Property management companies, apartment communities, commercial landlords, student housing, senior living
types.frequency: On vacancy, often clustered at lease cycle dates

termsIntro: Six words appear across commercial cleaning contracts as if they mean the same thing. They describe different outcomes, and the difference matters when a contract is written or an inspector reads one.

terms.means: Removes soil, dust, and organic matter with detergent and friction
terms.applies: Makes a surface visibly clean. Required before any disinfection step

terms.means: Reduces germs on a surface to a level public health standards consider safe
terms.applies: Common in food contact and childcare settings

terms.means: Kills specified pathogens using an EPA-registered product held at label contact time
terms.applies: Required in healthcare and during outbreaks

terms.means: The recurring contracted service that performs routine cleaning
terms.applies: Describes the contract and the crew, not a single task

terms.means: In-house staff performing the same routine work, usually in schools and municipal buildings
terms.applies: Describes employment model rather than a different scope

terms.means: The umbrella term for all paid cleaning of non-residential buildings
terms.applies: Includes janitorial work plus every specialist type on this list

steps.title: Set the recurring baseline first
steps.text: Decide what has to happen every service night. For most buildings that is janitorial or office cleaning. Everything else gets scheduled around it.

steps.title: Add the periodic work your surfaces need
steps.text: Hard floors, carpet, grout, glass, and high surfaces all degrade on their own cycle. Put each on a named frequency rather than calling it when someone notices.

steps.title: Check whether your industry changes the scope
steps.text: Healthcare, food service, childcare, and education carry requirements that turn a service list into a compliance document. Find out before you price it.

steps.title: Separate what needs a licensed or certified trade
steps.text: Hood and duct cleaning, grease trap pumping, and regulated medical waste are not general cleaning work. Assign them to the right contractor in writing.

steps.title: Match the schedule to your access window
steps.text: A scope that needs five hours in a three hour window fails every night. Fix the window, then size the scope to it.

steps.title: Write the quality check into the contract
steps.text: Agree a walkthrough schedule, who attends, and what happens when something fails. A monthly joint inspection with a signed sheet prevents most disputes.

faqs.q: What are the main types of commercial cleaning?
faqs.a: The recurring types are janitorial services, office cleaning, and day porter services. The periodic types are deep cleaning, floor care, carpet and tile work, window cleaning, and high dusting. The specialist types are medical, restaurant, school, warehouse, retail, hospitality, post-construction, event, and turnover cleaning.

faqs.q: What is the difference between janitorial and commercial cleaning?
faqs.a: Commercial cleaning is the umbrella term for all paid cleaning of non-residential buildings. Janitorial services is one type within it, specifically the recurring contracted work that happens on a set schedule. Every janitorial contract is commercial cleaning, but not all commercial cleaning is janitorial.

faqs.q: What is the difference between cleaning, sanitizing, and disinfecting?
faqs.a: Cleaning removes soil with detergent and friction. Sanitizing reduces germs to a level public health standards consider safe. Disinfecting kills specified pathogens using an EPA-registered product held wet for the contact time on the label. Surfaces must be cleaned before they can be disinfected.

faqs.q: How often should a commercial building be cleaned?
faqs.a: Most commercial buildings run nightly or several nights per week for routine janitorial work, with deep cleaning quarterly or semiannually and floor refinishing annually. Traffic volume, soil type, and regulatory requirements set the actual frequency, not building size.

faqs.q: What type of commercial cleaning does a medical office need?
faqs.a: A medical office needs medical facility cleaning, which uses risk zoning, color-coded equipment, EPA-registered disinfectants held at label contact times, and room-by-room documentation. Terminal cleaning is added for procedure and isolation rooms.

A day porter is a cleaner stationed in a building during operating hours who handles restrooms, spills, entries, and visible problems as they occur. Overnight janitorial crews clean an empty building; a day porter maintains an occupied one.

faqs.q: Is post-construction cleaning the same as deep cleaning?
faqs.a: No. Post-construction cleaning removes construction dust, adhesive, debris, and protective coverings from a new or renovated space, and it is a one-time job in staged visits. Deep cleaning is a recurring intensive clean of a building already in use.

faqs.q: Which industries need specialist commercial cleaning?
faqs.a: Healthcare, food service, childcare, education, food production, and laboratories all carry regulatory requirements that turn the cleaning scope into a compliance document. Warehousing, manufacturing, and hospitality need specialist equipment and scheduling rather than regulatory scope.

faqs.q: Can one cleaning company handle all of these types?
faqs.a: Most full-service commercial cleaning companies cover janitorial, office, deep cleaning, floor care, carpet, tile, and the major industry verticals. Kitchen hood and duct cleaning under NFPA 96, grease trap pumping, and regulated medical waste are separate licensed or certified trades.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right type of commercial cleaning for my building?
faqs.a: Start with the recurring baseline your building needs nightly, then add periodic types for the surfaces that degrade on a slower cycle, then check whether your industry carries a regulatory requirement that changes the scope. Most contracts end up as one recurring type plus two or three periodic ones.
